record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every polygonal billiard table have at least one periodic billiard orbit?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Does every polygon have a periodic orbit?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a polygon (a compact connected planar region bounded by finitely many straight line segments). The billiard flow on $P$ is the dynamical system that describes a point particle moving in straight lines inside $P$ with unit speed and reflecting elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) upon hitting the interior of an edge; trajectories that hit a vertex are left undefined. A billiard orbit is called periodic if, after finitely many reflections, the particle returns to its initial position with its initial velocity.

Prove or disprove: every polygon $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ admits at least one periodic billiard orbit.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely recognized as open. Even the restriction to triangles (the "triangular billiards conjecture") remains unresolved, although partial results are known: every rational polygon (vertex angles rational multiples of π) has dense periodic orbits, and various special classes of triangles (e.g., acute, right, and triangles with all angles less than 100°) are known to admit periodic orbits. The general polygonal case is listed among Katok's most resistant problems in dynamics.

status_evidence.snippet: The existence of periodic orbits in general polygonal billiards is a major open problem; even the triangle case is unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a periodic orbit in every polygonal billiard is open.

status_evidence.title: Classical and Open Problems about Billiard Dynamics (O. Knill)
status_evidence.snippet: Whether every polygon has a periodic billiard orbit is listed among the central open problems; Katok includes it among the most resistant problems.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is open and listed as a major problem by Katok.

status_evidence.title: Periodic billiard orbits in right triangles
status_evidence.snippet: Partial results establishing periodic orbits in special classes of triangles.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are available for triangles.
